clue.text: For this type of poisoning, kindly turn over to head-note

definitions.note: the clue describes the answer as a kind of poisoning; the answer is the noun naming it

blocks.note: PTO stands for 'please turn over', printed at the foot of a page
head as an adjective means chief or main
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A doctor's instructions for a poisoning case, with a polite request to turn the page to a note at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindly' stands for 'please', so 'kindly turn over' is the page-foot abbreviation PTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaine poisoning was the old name for food poisoning, blamed on compounds formed in decaying protein.

clue.text: Modify a style of painting

blocks.note: to temper is to moderate or modify
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter an artistic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a technique of painting with pigment bound in egg yolk, used widely before oils.

clue.text: Vermin catcher gets tramp out of the river

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are put in a fresh order
gets is read as takes in, so one piece receives another inside it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the Ouse is a river in England, a favourite crossword river

explanation.surface: A rat-catcher hauls a vagrant out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled tramp letters split around the river: the first one, then the river, then the other four.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousetrap is the spring device set to catch mice, the commonest household vermin.

clue.text: Know by instinct the in-thing that grabs a trade union

indicators.note: whatever grabs something holds it within its grip

blocks.note: IN means fashionable, and IT is 'the thing' in slang
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: Fashion trends somehow take over a workers' union, which anyone could sense.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is slang for the ultimate fashionable thing, as in 'the It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit something is to grasp it directly, without reasoning, by gut feeling.

clue.text: Letting a learner get involved in an amorous situation

indicators.note: things that get involved become tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Allowing a novice to become entangled in a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternal triangle is the classic romantic tangle of two people both attached to a third.

clue.text: He aims for the bull

blocks.note: surface reading: a darts player trying to hit the bullseye
setter's reading: the real animal in a ring, targeted by a bullfighter on foot

explanation.walkthrough: The bull of a dartboard is the natural first picture; the man really faces a live bull in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is a bullfighter, especially one who fights on foot, whose target is the animal itself.

clue.text: Its offspring has a long journey ahead

definitions.text: Its offspring has a long journey ahead

blocks.clueFragment: Its offspring has a long journey ahead
blocks.note: surface reading: some creature whose young must travel far
setter's reading: the child born on a particular weekday in the nursery rhyme that says this child has far to go

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face' gives each weekday's child a fate; one day's child 'has far to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional rhyme, Thursday's child has far to go, so this day's offspring faces a long road.

clue.text: Stop doctor boarding Eastern vessel

indicators.note: someone boarding goes inside a ship, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A port forbids a physician from getting on a ship from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command, but it is the noun: a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade or movement, a stop put on something.

clue.text: Strange oaths — very rash

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: Weird swearing is a sign of a reckless temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhasty means acting too quickly without thought, which is what rash describes.

clue.text: Quantity called for by Richard

definitions.note: read as two words, 'a mount', a horse

blocks.note: first meaning: a sum or quantity
second meaning: Shakespeare's Richard III cries 'A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!'

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words, an article and a horse to ride, and it is what Richard begs for on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a total or quantity of something; split, a mount is a riding horse.

clue.text: The point of the French measure can be taught

blocks.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
du is French for 'of the'
a cable is a nautical measure of length, a tenth of a sea mile

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the purpose of French measurement could be, and decides it can be learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Educable describes a person able to be educated, that is, capable of being taught.

clue.text: Change pattern of heartless sailors' flag

indicators.note: without a heart, the central letter is cut away

blocks.note: the Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships

explanation.surface: A merchant navy flag gets a new look after losing its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The flag's name has nine letters; its fifth, an N, is the heart that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign is to give something a new design, altering its pattern or layout.

clue.text: Stiffening for colourless Tudor Privy Council

indicators.note: colourless means with a colour taken out, so a colour word is removed

blocks.note: the Star Chamber was the court formed from the Privy Council under the Tudors

explanation.surface: A history note on what gave a Tudor court its rigid, drab character.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour removed is AMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is the substance used to stiffen collars and linen, so it is a stiffening agent.

clue.text: Turn away the composer

blocks.note: first meaning: to deflect a blow or thrust
second meaning: Sir Hubert ..., English composer of 'Jerusalem'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rejecting a composer; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing to parry is to ward off a stroke, and Hubert Parry wrote the music for 'Jerusalem'.

clue.text: Wild Pict imprisoning a group of country lovers

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, meaning 'typical of those who love their country'

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters run free into a new order
imprisoning shuts one thing up inside another

blocks.note: fodder: a Pict was one of the ancient peoples of Scotland
A plus TRIO, a group of three

explanation.surface: A savage ancient Scot locks up a band of nature-loving folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled Pict wraps round the group after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotic means devoted to one's country, which is what country lovers feel.

clue.text: Paradoxically, it's not a birdie!

blocks.note: surface reading: something that is no bird at all
setter's reading: in golf a birdie is one under par, and the score in question is three under, yet it is named after a large seabird

explanation.walkthrough: The paradox: this golf score is not a birdie, yet it is itself a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an albatross is three strokes under par on a hole; it is also a great ocean seabird.

clue.text: Having made amends, got into line again

blocks.note: first meaning: put right a wrong
second meaning: read as ..., soldiers dressing their ranks a second time

explanation.walkthrough: To dress ranks is a drill term for aligning soldiers, so doing it again is a second sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy it; to re-dress ranks is to straighten a military line again.

clue.text: Cracks a girl weeps about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to weep is to cry
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl sheds tears over fissures, perhaps in her house or her life.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl sits inside the weeping word, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crannies are small narrow openings or chinks, as in nooks and crannies.

clue.text: Marry poet? Maybe, but not till death do us part

definitions.text: not till death do us part

indicators.note: maybe signals one possible version, so these letters are rearranged in some way

blocks.note: fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: Someone considers wedding a poet, but only on a short-term basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the wedding vow: something not lasting till death is not permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporary means lasting only a limited time, the opposite of a lifelong vow.

clue.text: Restraint shown by master making a clean break

indicators.note: making a break smashes things, so the letters are broken up and reformed

blocks.note: M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA
fodder

explanation.surface: A prisoner's shackle is seen on a master who escapes cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal band or chain fastened round the wrist, a physical restraint.

clue.text: Pleased if youngster's content to improve morally

indicators.note: content means what is held inside, so the letters are within the words

blocks.note: the end of Pleased, all of if, and the start of youngster's

explanation.surface: A parent is glad when a child's satisfaction helps them become a better person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy' alongside 'Pleased', but here it means the contents of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct someone in a way that builds up their moral or intellectual character.

clue.text: A thrill for Friday's child

blocks.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday, with its 's
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Recalls the nursery rhyme in which each weekday's child has a fate; here one child gets an excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden brief shiver of excitement or emotion, which is a thrill.

clue.text: Have a kip in this French sofa

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: ce is French for 'this'
a kip is British slang for a sleep, so a kip is a nap

explanation.surface: An invitation to doze on a piece of French furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French sofa' reads as the definition, but 'French' goes with 'this' in the wordplay; the definition is just 'sofa'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a type of couch or settee, from the French word for that furniture.

clue.text: Order to charge to the Scot

blocks.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Someone is told to bill a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command; it is the noun, a classical or musical order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionian names a mode in music and, loosely, the Ionic order of classical architecture.

clue.text: Scholarly Irishman detailed to pursue a traitor

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with the tail cut off

blocks.note: taken as written
Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
Mick is a stock name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: A learned Irish detective is assigned to chase down a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To pursue' puts the Irishman after the traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic means relating to learning and scholarship, as in academic work.

clue.text: Food Heather's turning her hand to

blocks.note: tack is food, as in hard tack, a ship's biscuit
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather tries her hand at cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackling a task means setting about it, the same as turning one's hand to it.

clue.text: Rate for Jenny?

definitions.note: whimsical: a jenny is a she-ass, so a female ass might be an 'ass-ess'

blocks.note: first meaning: to value or evaluate
second meaning: a jenny is a female donkey, and -ess makes a feminine noun, as in lioness

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: an ass with the feminine ending -ess would be a jenny.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to rate or appraise something's value, while the joke reading is a female donkey.

clue.text: Parts of bodies in boxes

blocks.note: first meaning: the front of the torso
second meaning: large sturdy containers

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a grim discovery of body parts packed in crates; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the upper torso, and a large storage container is also called by this name.

clue.text: Correcting myself in winding up

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: winding up something is ending it
me stands for oneself, the speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to fixing their own mistakes while bringing things to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Emending a text means making corrections or revisions to it.
